verdict.rationale: Moneybird lets users create a personal API token and choose its scopes with checkboxes. It also supports OAuth with a token revocation endpoint, so credentials issued to an agent can be limited and revoked. The docs describe personal tokens as coming 'at a cost of security', and the actual scope list and its granularity are not shown. Missing for 10: the documented list of scopes and how fine-grained they are (e.g., read-only or per-resource), agent-specific credential guidance, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: For a personal API token, you can use the checkboxes to select the scopes you need.
you can create a personal API token that simplifies the setup
Moneybird supports the [OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7009) endpoint at `https://moneybird.com/oauth/revoke`.
